outline:
This course Linear Algebra
	is a mathematics course.
	is useful and fundamental to CSIE (and many other discipline) students.
	emphasizes both computations and concepts.
	asks you to use an open-source mathematical package called Scilab.
	guides you to read an English textbook.
	requires hard work.
schedule:
1. Linear Equations
	To understand the basic terminologies and notations of matrices and systems of linear equations, in the forms of vector equation and matrix equation.
	Solving a system of linear equations with the Gaussian elimination: reducing a matrix to its echelon form.
	To interpret a system of linear equations in various ways.
	First exposure to key concepts such as linear independence and linear transformation.
2. Matrix Algebra
	To learn basic matrix arithmetic operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication power, transpose, and inverse.
	To summarize the concepts for systems of n linear equations in n unknowns.
3. Vector Spaces
	Introduction to vector spaces.
	Fundamental subspaces of a matrix: column space, row space, and null space.
	Basis and dimension of a vector space.
4. Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
	To find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix.
	Diagonalization of a matrix (linear transformation).
5. Orthogonality and Orthogonal Bases
	To introduce inner product of vectors, and thus the geometric concepts of length, distance, and angle (perpendicularity).
	To be familiar with the use of orthogonal bases.
	Least-Squares approximation.
assessment:
1. Attendance and warm-up quizzes (sampled and comprehensive), 10% (extra).
2. Written exercises, 20%. Hand in your homework every Thursday right before class.
3. Programming assignments and Scilab projects, 20%.
For 2 and 3, discussion is encouraged but plagiarization (抄襲) is prohibited.
4. Two 50-minute tests, 10% each. (20%)
5. Midterm exam and final exam, 20% each. (40%)
